sources.citation: Lubbe, Melissa, Tiffany Priest & Sigrid Lew. 2022. A preliminary phonology and Latin-based orthography of Para Naga (Jejara), Northwest Myanmar. Journal of the Southeast Asian Linguistics Society 15(2).

sources.note: Sister language (Para Naga) in the same Payap/SIL Myanmar Naga project; may contain comparative notes on Makuri prosody and cites the survey literature; open access on eVols but download could not be reached by automated download.

sources.citation: van Dam, Kellen Parker. 2026. Patkaian (Northern Naga). Oxford handbook chapter (Zenodo 22253033).
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Mentions Makuri once, only as a contact source for Paung Nyuan ('the number one khat', line 1087); nothing on Makuri phonology or stress.

sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: No phonology at all; only classification, dialects (Shi 2009:5 lists Phuvle, Makheotle, Sengphuvle, Muvle, Jeile) and bibliography (Shi 2009; Shintani 2018; LSDO 2006; Saul 2005; Hsiu 2021).

sources.citation: Glottolog 5.3 languoid page maku1273 (and Glottolog 5.1 CLDF values/sources held by the project
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Nothing on stress. Lists exactly two references for maku1273: Shi 2009 (MA thesis; Glottolog's fullest description is a phonology or text collection) and Naga Survey Team 2006 (Ms.). Alternative names Makury Naga, Shaera.

sources.citation: Shintani, Tadahiko L.A. 2018. The Makuri language. Linguistic survey of Tay cultural area no. 117. Fuchu: ILCAA. 24+268 pp. ISBN 978-4-86337-283-2.
sources.tag: likely states stress; not yet obtained
sources.access_detail: print only (no digital copy found when the work was looked up)
sources.note: Largest primary description of Makuri (268-page wordlist with a phonological introduction, in English); LSTCA introductions describe the tone system and would be the place to find any statement on stress/accent.

sources.citation: Shi, Vong Tsuh. 2009. Discourse studies of Makuri Naga narratives. MA thesis, Payap University, Chiang Mai. xiii+168 pp.
sources.tag: likely states stress; not yet obtained
sources.access_detail: not located online or in the libraries checked
sources.note: The only descriptive work Glottolog rates at phonology/text level; Payap discourse theses conventionally open with a phonology summary (phonemes, tones, syllable) that may state whether Makuri is tonal and whether stress plays a role. Also identifies the dialect described.

sources.citation: Naga Survey Team (Language and Social Development Organization). 2006. A sociolinguistic survey of Makuri, Para, and Long Phuri Naga in Layshi Township, Myanmar. Unpublished ms.
sources.tag: likely states stress; not yet obtained
sources.note: Second of the two Glottolog references; sociolinguistic and lexicostatistic only, unlikely to state stress but is the wordlist basis for the 93%/30-37% similarity figures and names the varieties.
